label: Google Calendar
description: Arcade.dev LLM tools for Google Calendar

tools.name: CreateEvent
tools.description:
Create a new event/meeting/sync/meetup in the specified calendar.

Pass `recurrence` to create a repeating event.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: The title of the event

parameters.name: start_datetime
parameters.description: When the event starts. For a timed event, a datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). For an all-day event, a date (YYYY-MM-DD); end_datetime must then be a date too.

parameters.name: end_datetime
parameters.description: When the event ends. For a timed event, a datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). For an all-day event, a date (YYYY-MM-DD) that is exclusive: the day after the event's last day. A date equal to start_datetime creates a single all-day event on that day.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The ID of the calendar to create the event in. Defaults to 'primary'.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: The description of the event. Defaults to no description.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: The location of the event. Defaults to no location.

parameters.name: visibility
parameters.description: The visibility of the event. Defaults to default, which uses the calendar's default visibility.

parameters.name: attendee_emails
parameters.description: The list of attendee emails. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com. Defaults to no attendees.

parameters.name: send_notifications_to_attendees
parameters.description: Which guests Google emails an invitation to. externalOnly emails only guests who do not use Google Calendar. Defaults to all.

parameters.name: add_google_meet
parameters.description: Whether to add a Google Meet link to the event. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: recurrence
parameters.description: Recurrence rules for a repeating event, in RFC 5545 format. Each entry is an RRULE/RDATE/EXDATE line; a bare rule is automatically prefixed with 'RRULE:'. Examples: ['RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;COUNT=10'] for every Mon/Wed/Fri for 10 occurrences, or ['RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;UNTIL=YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ'] for daily until a UTC date-time. Defaults to a one-time event.

output.description: A dictionary containing the created event details

description.value: Weekly sync to discuss project updates, blockers, and upcoming milestones.

location.value: Conference Room B, 123 Main St, San Francisco, CA 94105

tools.name: FindTimeSlotsWhenEveryoneIsFree
tools.description: Provide time slots when everyone is free within a given date range and time boundaries.

parameters.name: email_addresses
parameters.description: The list of email addresses from people in the same organization domain (apart from the currently logged in user) to search for free time slots. Defaults to the current user only.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: The start date to search for time slots in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. It will search starting from this date at the time 00:00:00. Defaults to today's date.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: The end date to search for time slots in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. It will search until this date at the time 23:59:59. Defaults to 7 days from today.

parameters.name: start_time_boundary
parameters.description: Will return free slots in any given day starting from this time in the format 'HH:MM'. Defaults to '08:00', which is a usual business hour start time.

parameters.name: end_time_boundary
parameters.description: Will return free slots in any given day until this time in the format 'HH:MM'. Defaults to '18:00', which is a usual business hour end time.

output.description: A dictionary with the free slots and the timezone in which time slots are represented.

tools.name: GetEvent
tools.description:
Get one Google Calendar event by its id.

When the event is one occurrence of a recurring series, the series' repeat rule and first
start are returned too, so read them here before changing or ending a series. The rule
counts from series_start, not from this occurrence's start. Use this instead of
listing a time window whenever the event id is already known. Deleted events and deleted
occurrences are still returned, with a cancelled status.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the event. For a recurring event, pass an occurrence's id to read that occurrence along with its series' repeat rule, or the series id to read the series itself.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The identifier of the calendar that holds the event. Defaults to 'primary', the authenticated user's main calendar.

output.description: The event's details, and the repeat rule and first start of its series

tools.description: List all calendars accessible by the user.

parameters.name: max_results

parameters.description: Whether to show deleted calendars. Defaults to False

parameters.name: show_hidden
parameters.description: Whether to show hidden calendars. Defaults to False

parameters.name: next_page_token
parameters.description: The token to retrieve the next page of calendars. Defaults to the first page.

output.description: A dictionary containing the calendars accessible by the end user

tools.name: ListEvents
tools.description:
List events from the specified calendar within the given datetime range.

min_end_datetime serves as the lower bound (exclusive) for an event's end time.
max_start_datetime serves as the upper bound (exclusive) for an event's start time.

For example, with min_end_datetime at 09:00 on one day and max_start_datetime at
17:00 the next day, the function returns events that:
1. End after 09:00 on the first day (exclusive)
2. Start before 17:00 on the second day (exclusive)
So an event from 08:00 to 10:00 on the first day is included, but an event
starting at 17:00 on the second day is not.

parameters.name: min_end_datetime
parameters.description: Filter by events that end on or after this datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS).

parameters.name: max_start_datetime
parameters.description: Filter by events that start before this datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS).

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The ID of the calendar to list events from. Defaults to 'primary'.

parameters.name: max_results
parameters.description: The maximum number of events to return. Defaults to 10.

output.description: A dictionary containing the list of events

tools.description:
Accept, decline, or tentatively accept (RSVP to) a meeting invitation on the
authenticated user's behalf.

Sets the user's responseStatus for an event they were invited to.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The ID of the event to respond to. Use an event's id from an event listing to respond to a single occurrence of a recurring event, or its recurringEventId to respond to the whole series.

parameters.name: response

tools.name: UpdateEvent
tools.description:
Update an existing event in the specified calendar with the provided details.
Only the provided fields will be updated; others will remain unchanged.
Pass `updated_calendar_id` to move the event to another calendar.

An event's details can only be changed by the event's organizer, or by a guest
when the organizer has enabled guest editing for that event.

`updated_start_datetime` and `updated_end_datetime` are
independent and can be provided separately, except that all-day
dates must be provided for both.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The ID of the event to update

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The ID of the calendar containing the event. Defaults to 'primary'.

parameters.name: updated_start_datetime
parameters.description: The updated start of the event. For a timed event, a datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). For an all-day event, a date (YYYY-MM-DD); updated_end_datetime must then be a date too. Defaults to leaving the start unchanged.

parameters.name: updated_end_datetime
parameters.description: The updated end of the event. For a timed event, a datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). For an all-day event, a date (YYYY-MM-DD) that is exclusive: the day after the event's last day. A date equal to updated_start_datetime makes it a single all-day event on that day. Defaults to leaving the end unchanged.

parameters.name: updated_calendar_id
parameters.description: The ID of a calendar to move the event to. The event is moved there after the other updates are applied. Defaults to keeping the event on its current calendar.

parameters.name: updated_summary
parameters.description: The updated title of the event. Defaults to leaving the title unchanged.

parameters.name: updated_description
parameters.description: The updated description of the event. Defaults to leaving the description unchanged.

parameters.name: updated_location
parameters.description: The updated location of the event. Defaults to leaving the location unchanged.

parameters.name: updated_visibility
parameters.description: The visibility of the event. Defaults to leaving the visibility unchanged.

parameters.name: updated_recurrence
parameters.description: Updated recurrence rules for a repeating event, in RFC 5545 format. Each entry is an RRULE/RDATE/EXDATE line; a bare rule is automatically prefixed with 'RRULE:'. Provide the full set of rules to replace the event's existing recurrence, e.g. ['RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;COUNT=10'] for every Mon/Wed/Fri for 10 occurrences. Pass an empty list ([]) to REMOVE recurrence and make the event a one-time event. Defaults to leaving recurrence unchanged.

parameters.name: attendee_emails_to_add
parameters.description: The list of attendee emails to add. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com. Defaults to adding no attendees.

parameters.name: attendee_emails_to_remove
parameters.description: The list of attendee emails to remove. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com. Defaults to removing no attendees.

parameters.name: send_notifications_to_attendees
parameters.description: Which guests Google emails about the update. externalOnly emails only guests who do not use Google Calendar. Defaults to all.

parameters.name: updated_google_meet
parameters.description: Add or remove the event's Google Meet link. Defaults to leaving the link unchanged.

output.description: A string containing the updated event details, including the event ID, update timestamp, and a link to view the updated event.

updated_description.value: Quarterly review of strategy and OKRs for all team leads. Please come prepared with your department updates.

updated_location.value: Conference Room B, 123 Main St, San Francisco, CA 94105

summary:
## Google Calendar Toolkit

The Google Calendar toolkit lets Arcade-powered LLM agents read, create, and manage Google Calendar data on behalf of authenticated users.

## Capabilities

- **Calendar discovery & user context** — list all calendars the user can access and retrieve full profile/permission details for the authenticated account.
- **Event retrieval** — fetch a single event by ID (including recurrence rules and cancelled/deleted occurrences) or list events across a flexible datetime window with precise boundary semantics.
- **Event creation & recurrence** — create one-off or repeating events with full recurrence rule support.
- **Event editing & moving** — update any subset of event fields on an existing event, or move it to a different calendar; respects organizer and guest-editing permissions.
- **RSVP & deletion** — accept, tentatively accept, or decline meeting invitations on the user's behalf, and delete events from a calendar.
- **Scheduling assistance** — find free time slots across multiple attendees within a given date range and daily time boundaries.

## OAuth

This toolkit authenticates via **OAuth 2.0** through the Google provider. See the [Arcade Google auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/google) for setup instructions.
